definitions.explanation: A thin, absorbent paper used for Japanese calligraphy (書道). Standard size is approximately 24cm × 33cm. Named because it is roughly half the size of a full sheet of traditional Japanese paper.

examples.japanese: {半紙|はんし}に{筆|ふで}で{書|か}く。
examples.english: To write on calligraphy paper with a brush.

examples.japanese: {書道|しょどう}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{半紙|はんし}を{使|つか}う。
examples.english: We use calligraphy paper in calligraphy class.

examples.japanese: {百均|ひゃっきん}で{半紙|はんし}を{買|か}ってきたが、{墨|すみ}の{乗|の}りがあまり{良|よ}くなかった。
examples.english: I bought calligraphy paper at the hundred-yen store, but the ink didn't adhere very well.

notes:
USAGE:
Familiar to all Japanese people from {書道|しょどう} (calligraphy) classes in school. The paper is designed to absorb ink from a {筆|ふで} (brush). Quality varies widely — practice paper is inexpensive, while high-quality {半紙|はんし} for exhibitions can be costly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {半紙|はんし}に{書|か}く (to write on calligraphy paper)
- {練習用|れんしゅうよう}{半紙|はんし} (practice calligraphy paper)
- {半紙|はんし}を{広|ひろ}げる (to spread out calligraphy paper)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {和紙|わし}: Japanese paper — the broader category of traditional Japanese paper
- {画用紙|がようし}: drawing paper — thicker paper for painting and drawing
